analyzed_vuln.description: Use-after-free caused by incorrect shutdown order: zend_deactivate() calls shutdown_executor() before shutdown_compiler(). shutdown_executor() iterates EG(function_table) and dereferences zend_op_array entries (e.g., op_array->type/static_variables), but those op_array structures can still point into compiler arena memory (CG(arena)). shutdown_compiler() then destroys CG(arena), and the observed PoV reaches a state where shutdown_executor reads data that has already been freed from that arena region, producing a heap UAF (crash site in shutdown_executor at zend_execute_API.c:285). Root cause is lifetime/teardown sequencing in zend_deactivate, not just the read instruction itself.
analyzed_vuln.conditions: Trigger requires a request that creates user-function op_array/compiler-managed data in CG(arena) (the parser fuzzer input does this via malformed/complex PHP code), then reaches request shutdown. During php_request_shutdown -> zend_deactivate, executor shutdown walks function/class tables and touches op_array fields while compiler arena-backed memory has become invalid for that path, leading to dereference of freed arena memory. No special external state is needed beyond crafted script input that leaves such entries reachable at shutdown.
